account: Today has seemed routine so far; I have not witnessed anything clearly unusual or received confirmed public news. This morning I read my appointments at town hall. The secretary asked to review the appointment book to prepare meetings, and I gave it over; I later saw the secretary return it to the appointments chest. That appears to be ordinary scheduling work. During my ten o'clock market walk I visited the stalls, bought a fresh loaf, and sought news. Townsfolk 08 and 30 said they had none. My neighbour described a pleasant morning of strolling and greetings at the bakery, also with no confirmed news. We confirmed our usual three o'clock tea at the cottage at (16, -60, 105), beside the east ferry landing. I have now arrived home for the noon lunch appointment. Next comes town accounts at the office at one, tea at three, office again at four-thirty, and home at seven. Nothing I have observed gives me grounds to infer a hidden purpose or unusual activity.
